findings.issue: Commit 6b536038 changed CommittedCommandResponseFilter so it sets x-idempotency-key only when the key is non-empty (line 98). This repairs cycle-1 nonblocking finding 5, but no integration or unit test checks the header on the wire. Nothing asserts that a 403/400/500 CommandRejectionResponse omits x-idempotency-key, or that committed and replayed responses carry the request key. In the four header rules, allowlisted-header replay, content-type only with bytes, and idempotency-replayed only on replay are each asserted at least once. The key-header rule is asserted nowhere, so a regression back to an empty header would go unnoticed.
findings.required_change: Inspector: in transactional-command-provenance.integration.spec.ts (wrong-order 403) or transactional-command-http.spec.ts, assert Object.hasOwn(rejection.headers, 'x-idempotency-key') === false on a boundary rejection. Also assert that committed and replayed responses echo the request key in x-idempotency-key. Then have the Architect rebind law/trace.json. This can be done during CTG6–CTG8 hardening and does not block ordered import.

summary: HEAD is 7e858d57ca1fd72b0c7f0a3fb44dbfbbedcadc06, and the tree is clean apart from two untracked temp files. The repair commits are role-separated. 38fe9477 is the Architect triage. 674c43e3 (Inspector) touches tests only. 6b536038 (Engineer) touches only the command source and the changeset in the fixed group. ffbf3426 and 7e858d57 are Architect plan checkpoints that record predecessor SHAs, focal PASS counts and the DDL/seed disposition. f9fa42d6 is the Architect trace rebind. Checked locally: check:trace passes with 430/430 bound, api:baselines matches 44/44, and the tenancy unit spec passes 6/6. The five backend CTG5 specs pass 32/32 over real Nest HTTP and PostgreSQL; I did not rerun the full local CI. Blocking finding 1 is repaired: the new provenance spec runs StynxTenancyModule with two Host tenants. It commits nominal public commands (configured actor) and verified optional-auth public commands (verified actor) on stynx_app with per-tenant audit rows and keys, and replays byte-identical responses. Visible audit rows and keys are limited to the request's own tenant. A protected command commits only after the port attests membership. The core → command → tenancy order returns 403 COMMAND_TENANT_PROVENANCE_INVALID with no handler call, no requireActor transaction, no key and no audit row. Bootstrap rejects a missing tenancy port, a same-name look-alike guard, a subclass that only inherits the brand, and a guard registered only through useGlobalGuards. Blocking finding 2 is repaired: catchesCommitted now matches by prototype, so a filter that catches Error, HttpException, IntrinsicException or everything counts for both CommittedCommandResponse and CommandRejectionResponse. Real HTTP tests reject bootstrap for @Catch() and @Catch(Error) when the consumer filter would come first. With the consumer filter in the other order, a committed 502 and its replay go out on the wire with identical bytes, JSON content-type, idempotency-replayed and one handler call. This matches Nest's reversed selection of method filters; class and global filters are selected after method filters. The nonblocking findings are handled. The REVOKE of audit.write is documented in the changeset. The DDL/seed disposition names test/db/transactional-commands-migration.spec.ts as the sensor. The empty key header is now omitted, though no test covers that (see above). The bootstrap walks inherited methods, and a real test rejects an inherited unguarded route. Both bounded-wait race outcomes are tested: when the winner commits during the wait, the contender gets a byte-identical replay; when the winner rolls back, the contender acquires the key. The earlier assertions are unchanged in substance: the removed expect lines were reformatted, and toBeUndefined was replaced by equivalent or stricter checks. That covers the statement-timeout rollback with a 5xx that is not 409 and handler count equal to attempts, the separate lock-timeout-only IN_PROGRESS path, and audit contention not labelled IN_PROGRESS. All other conclusions from cycle 1 still hold on this HEAD. The remaining gaps are small test additions and do not block safe ordered import into the cumulative branch under OD-S15-02.
